races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Beth Helfrich
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented North Carolina House District 98 (Davidson, Cornelius, Huntersville) since January 2025. Davidson College graduate. Worked as an English teacher and school administrator from 2005 to 2020, then at a local bookstore and as a writer/editor with her own writing company.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed among her 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations on Ballotpedia.

In her 2026 Ballotpedia survey she lists endorsements from the Charlotte Observer, NC Police Benevolent Association, NCAE, Charlotte-Metrolina Labor Council/AFL-CIO, Everytown for Gun Safety, EMILY's List, Planned Parenthood Votes South Atlantic and NC League of Conservation Voters, among others. This list is self-reported.

cands.gaps: We could not find her city or town of birth. We found no specific bills she sponsored with their numbers or details, so her claims about authoring zoning, IVF and public-safety bills are unverified. We found no documented stance from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on institutional or foreign land buyers, immigration enforcement or H-1B, police pay and pensions, or school vouchers and teacher pay. We found no controversies, foreign ties or notable news coverage about her in the pages available.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as North Carolina, and she describes herself as a third-generation northern Mecklenburg resident, a North Mecklenburg High School graduate, and a parent raising five children less than a mile from her childhood home.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since January 2025 (one term plus re-election). Before that she was a teacher and school administrator for nearly two decades (2005–2020), then worked at a bookstore and ran a writing company. She also co-owns a family small business and was a school PTO president.
qual.why: She holds legislative office now, but only about two years of service. Her career was in education and writing, with no law, policy or budget career, so she scores in the upper-middle range.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her campaign site says she has authored bills that would protect local zoning control, and lists responsible growth among her priorities.

pro-life.evidence: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey she said she would work to expand access to quality healthcare, childcare and reproductive care, and listed reproductive care among her policy passions.

second-amendment.evidence: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey she listed gun violence prevention as a policy passion and said she would demand common-sense legislation to keep kids safer at home and in school.

cands.name: John Rhodes
cands.bio: John Rhodes was the Republican nominee for North Carolina House District 98 in 2026. He advanced unopposed after the canceled March 2026 primary and lost the general election to incumbent Democrat Beth Gardner Helfrich. His occupation and offices held are not documented in the sources reviewed.
cands.gaps: We could not find where John Rhodes was born or raised, when he came to North Carolina, or his career and any offices he has held. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and we found no campaign statements, platform positions, or documented stances on data centers or development. We found no endorsements, no controversies, and no foreign ties. The only page we had was his Ballotpedia profile, which lists his race and result but gives no biographical detail.
